newsitem.title: USA: USWC crudes up with WTI, ANS discount unconfirmed.
newsitem.headline: USWC crudes up with WTI, ANS discount unconfirmed.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices edged up Tuesday with West Texas Intermediate (WTI) values, while discounts remained stagnant as traders tried to confirm an Alaskan crude deal that went unreported last week.
Most West Coast crude traders heard a BP sold a second cargo of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude last week at a discount wider than the $1.05 reported.
BP and Exxon denied selling the cargo, but U.S. Oil, the alleged buyer, declined to comment when asked if they purchased the crude.
Outright ANS rose 20 cents to $18.33/18.53 a barrel.
Two shut pipelines on IPL Energy's pipeline into the U.S. began flowing at low rates Tuesday after power was restored to two pumping stations in the U.S. Midwest.
Officials at Canada's Trans Mountain Pipe Line, which can divert excess crude to the Pacific Northwest, said they did not receive requests to ship more crude.
California heavy and light grades remained flat early Monday.
